daily_quests.title: ASX 200 Stock Performance Rankings with Window Functions
daily_quests.description: Using the ASX 200 historical prices dataset, write a SQL query with window functions to rank stocks by their 30-day average return within each sector. Use ROW_NUMBER() to identify the top performer per sector, LAG() to calculate day-over-day price changes, and a CTE to compute the 30-day moving average. Return: stock_code, sector, closing_price, 30day_avg_return, rank_in_sector, previous_day_close. Filter for the last 90 days of data and order by sector and rank.

daily_quests.title: NSW Road Crash Data Cleaning & Injury Classification Pipeline
daily_quests.description: Download the NSW Road Crash Data (data.nsw.gov.au). Build a Python/pandas script that: (1) loads the CSV and identifies missing values per column; (2) standardises datetime formats for crash_date and crash_time; (3) creates a new column injury_severity by mapping injury counts to categories (no_injury, minor, serious, fatal); (4) removes duplicate rows based on crash_id; (5) filters for crashes in the Sydney metropolitan area only; (6) exports the cleaned dataset to a new CSV with timestamp in filename. Log the number of rows removed at each step.

daily_quests.title: AIHW Health Expenditure Trend Analysis: Python ETL → SQL Analytics
daily_quests.description: Using AIHW health expenditure data: (1) Write a Python script using pandas to load the CSV, clean column names (remove spaces, standardise to snake_case), handle missing values by forward-filling by state and year, and add a new column real_expenditure_2020_dollars using a fixed CPI deflator. Export to a staging CSV. (2) Load the cleaned data into a SQL database (SQLite or PostgreSQL). (3) Write a SQL query using window functions to calculate year-over-year expenditure growth % by state, rank states by growth, and use LAG() to compare each year to the previous. Return: state, year, expenditure_2020_dollars, yoy_growth_pct, state_rank. Identify the top 3 states with highest average growth over the period.
